technical-data.invention-title: INTERFEROMETER COUPLER USING MULTIPLE INPUT PORTS FOR IMPROVED STABIBLITY
COUPLEUR D'INTERFEROMETRE UTILISANT DES PORTS D'ENTREE MULTIPLES AFIN D'AMELIORER LA STABILITE

abstract.p: A multiport bidirectional coupler (31) is interconnected to a two beam interferometer (30), such as a Sagnac interferometer. Light from a source (40) is input into each of the ports (32-34) of the coupler (31) in turn. For each input the corresponding output intensities from all ports (32-34) are each mesured by a detector (39). By optical reciprocity, cyclic sums formed from the measured output allow an accurate estimation of the phase shift of the interferometer (30) independently of small deviations of the coupler parameters from ideal values. Thus instabilities of the coupler (31), due for example to age or temperature, are compensated for. A single pulse from the source (40) can be used to sequentially interrogate the interferometer (30) through each of the ports (32-34) in turn, by using additional couplers (35-38) and delay loops (41-44) to temporally stream the input and output signals.

Cette invention concerne un coupleur bidirectionnel à ports multiples (31) qui est interconnecté à un interféromètre à deux faisceaux (30), tel qu'un interféromètre de Sagnac. La lumière provenant d'une source (40) est introduite tour à tour dans chaque port (32 34) du coupleur (31). Pour chaque entrée, les intensités de sortie correspondantes de tous les ports (32 34) sont chacune mesurées par un détecteur (39). Par réciprocité optique, les sommes cycliques formées par les émissions mesurées permettent d'estimer précisément le décalage de phase de l'interféromètre (30) indépendamment des petits écarts des paramètres du coupleur par rapport aux valeurs idéales. Il est ainsi possible de compenser les instabilités du coupleur (31) qui sont par exemple dues à l'âge ou à la température. Une impulsion unique provenant de la source (40) permet d'interroger séquentiellement l'interféromètre (30) tour à tour par chacun des ports (32 34), ceci en utilisant des coupleurs complémentaires (35 38) et des boucles de retardement (41 44) afin de transférer temporairement les signaux d'entrée et de sortie.

description.p: INTERFEROMETER COUPLER USING MULTIPLE INPUT PORTS FOR IMPROVED STABIBLITY
Field of the Invention
The present invention is directed to the field of optical signal processing and in particular to the processing of interferometric signals utilising a coupler or the like.
Background of the Invention

Sagnac interferometric techniques are often utilised in various measurement fields including optical gyroscopes and current measuring devices. For example, PCT Application No. PCT/AU92/000680 by Clarke discloses one form of current sensor device utilising interferometric techniques. These devices utilise a coupler for coupling optical signals into and out of the overall Sagnac arrangement. The basic form of a current sensor according to Clarke includes a Sagnac loop attached to a 3 x 3 coupler with the coupler being utilised to couple optical signals in and out of the Sagnac loop. An optical source injects light via the coupler bidirectionally around the Sagnac loop with the output on each arm of the coupler being measured by detectors .

The arrangement utilising the 3 x 3 coupler is used to measure rotation (gyroscope) or magnetic fields (current sensor) . The arrangement is a passive interferometer in that it contains no active optical elements for modulating frequency, phase or amplitude. In such a passive system, the stability of the optical components is critical. Unfortunately, in practice the 3 x 3 coupler has been known to change its coupling parameters with temperature and time. Summary of the Invention
It is an object of at least preferred embodiments of the present invention to provide for an improved form of interrogating a Sagnac interferometer.

In accordance with a first aspect of the present invention, there is provided a method of interrogating an
optical coupler interconnected to a two beam interferometer, so as to determine an idealised output value, said optical coupler having a number of bidirectional external input/output ports, said method comprising the steps of: for each of said external input/output ports: inserting an optical signal into the port, measuring a corresponding output at each of said ports, forming a summation of said corresponding outputs; and determining said idealized output value of said coupler from said summations.

The optical coupler can comprise a 3 x 3 coupler and each of the summations can be formed from a corresponding output from each of the ports for a particular optical signal insertion. The two beam interferometer can comprise a Sagnac interferometer .
The two beam interferometer can comprise a Michelson interferometer.
In one implementation, the summations are formed from a single optical pulse appropriately delayed so that said corresponding outputs arrive at a detector in a temporally spaced manner.

In accordance with a second aspect of the present invention there is provided an apparatus for interrogating an optical coupler interconnected to a two beam interferometer, so as to determine an idealised output value, said optical coupler having a number of bidirectional external input/output ports, said apparatus comprising: means for inserting optical signals into each of the ports; means for measuring a corresponding output at each of said ports when an optical signal is inserted into one of the ports; and means for forming a summation of said corresponding outputs.
The apparatus may further comprise means for determining the idealised output value of the coupler from said summations.

Detailed Description of the Preferred and Other Embodiments

As shown in Fig. 1, in a Sagnac interferometer closed by a 3 x 3 coupler 10 there are three external ports labelled 1, 2 and 3 and ports u, v, w; two (u, v) of which close the Sagnac loop, while w may be unused. If the coupler 10 is ideal in the sense that it is lossless and the splitting ratios are all exactly 1/3, then any of the three external ports will do as an input port and no additional information is obtained by using more than one input port. If the coupler has small losses and the splitting ratios differ by small amounts from the ideal value 1/3, additional information can be obtained by using more than one input port.

By using all three input ports, the effects of small departures from ideal coupler parameters can be eliminated to the first order, or at least reduced to a single parameter expressing an average excess loss for the coupler. The theoretical basis of this processing is the principle of reciprocity, which connects the forward and reverse transition amplitudes in the coupler. The analysis ignores polarisation, that is, it is a scalar theory. It is however substantially applicable to a system in which polarisation filtering is employed so that there is in effect only a single polarisation state in the system. One form of arrangement using the aforementioned principles is illustrated in Fig. 2. In this system, the Sagnac loop 30 is interconnected to a 3 x 3 coupler 31 which is in turn interconnected to input/output couplers 32-3 . The couplers 32-34 are in turn connected by the couplers 35, 36, 37, 38. Hence, the output from optical source 40 is coupled by coupler 36 immediately to coupler arm 34 and after a delay by fibre delay loop 41 to coupler 35. The output from coupler 35 is immediately forwarded to coupler 33 and delayed by delay loop 42 before being sent to coupler 32. The outputs from the coupler 31 are again time delayed by means of delay loops 43, 44 so as to have a staggered temporal return to detector 39. In this manner, a pulsed output from source 40 can be temporally monitored at detector 39 to determine the summations of equation 19.
In this manner, the Sagnac interferometer can be sequentially interrogated through each of the three inputs. The outputs are processed in the manner described.

claim.claim-text: 1. A method of interrogating an optical coupler interconnected to a two beam interferometer, so as to determine an idealised output value, said optical coupler having a number of bidirectional external input/output ports, said method comprising the steps of: for each of said external input/output ports : inserting an optical signal into the port; measuring a corresponding output at each of said ports; forming a summation of said corresponding outputs; and determining said idealized output value of said coupler from said summations.
2. A method as claimed in claim 1, whereby the property of reciprocity is possessed by the summed outputs, whereby the signal is accurately zero when the measurement current or rotation) is zero.
3. A method as claimed in claims 1 or 2 wherein the number of the external input/output ports is equal to or greater than 3.
4. A method as claimed in claim 3 wherein said optical coupler comprises a 3 x 3 coupler.

5. A method as claimed in any previous claim wherein each of said summations is formed from a corresponding output from each of the ports for a particular optical signal insertion. 6. A method as claimed in any previous claim wherein said two beam interferometer comprises a Sagnac interferometer .

7. A method as claimed in any previous claim wherein said summations are formed from a single optical pulse appropriately delayed so that said corresponding outputs arrive at a detector in a temporally spaced manner.

8. An apparatus for interrogating an optical
coupler interconnected to a two beam interferometer, so as to determine an idealised output value, said optical coupler having a number of bidirectional external input/output ports, said apparatus comprising: means for inserting optical signals into each of the ports; means for measuring a corresponding output at each of said ports when an optical signal is inserted into one of the ports; and means for forming a summation of said corresponding outputs.
9. An apparatus as claimed in claim 8, further comprising means for determining the idealised output value of the coupler from said summations.
